name: ipconfig
desc: Display and manage Windows IP configuration for all network adapters.

usage.cmt: full details: MAC, DHCP server, lease times, DNS
flush DNS resolver cache — fix stale DNS

quick_flags.desc: show full details including MAC and DHCP info

scenarios: Machine can't reach the internet — check if IP is APIPA (169.254.x.x) which means DHCP failed
DNS caching old IP after a server migration
Gathering network info for a support ticket

mistakes.x: Running ipconfig without /all misses critical details
mistakes.fix: Always use /all — shows MAC, DHCP status, DNS servers, and lease info

mistakes.x: Forgetting to flush DNS after changing hosts file
mistakes.fix: ipconfig /flushdns must be run after editing hosts or after DNS changes

tags: ip address network adapter dns dhcp lease windows configuration

name: netstat (Windows)
desc: Display active TCP connections, listening ports, and Ethernet statistics on Windows.

usage.cmt: all connections with PID, no DNS resolution
correlate PID from netstat to process name

quick_flags.desc: show all connections and listening ports

scenarios: Application won't start — port already in use
Find which process is using a specific port
Detecting unexpected outbound connections during IR

mistakes.x: netstat without -o hides PIDs
mistakes.fix: Use -ano always — PID column is essential for identifying the owning process

mistakes.x: Not correlating PID to process name
mistakes.fix: Follow up with tasklist /fi "pid eq PID" to get the actual executable name

secnote: During Windows IR: netstat -ano combined with tasklist shows what is communicating. Flag any process making outbound connections that shouldn't be (svchost to external IPs, etc.).
tags: netstat windows port connection pid listening tcp udp network

name: tasklist / taskkill
desc: List running processes (tasklist) and terminate them (taskkill). Windows equivalent of ps/kill.

usage.cmt: list all running processes with PID and memory
show which services are running inside each process

quick_flags.desc: show hosted services for each process
verbose — show full path and window title

scenarios: Application frozen — identify PID and force kill it
Finding resource-hungry processes before a maintenance window
Identifying which svchost instance is hosting a misbehaving service

mistakes.x: taskkill without /f may fail on unresponsive processes
mistakes.fix: Add /f to force terminate; some processes require it

mistakes.x: Killing svchost.exe without checking /svc first
mistakes.fix: svchost hosts multiple services — run tasklist /svc to find the right one

tags: process list kill terminate pid windows tasklist taskkill

name: sfc / DISM
desc: System File Checker (sfc) and DISM repair Windows system file corruption.

usage.cmt: scan and repair corrupted system files (run as admin)

quick_flags.desc: scan and automatically repair protected system files
DISM: repair image from Windows Update

scenarios: After malware removal — system behaving strangely
Blue screen or random crashes after an update
Applications failing with missing DLL errors

mistakes.x: Running sfc without admin rights — silently fails
mistakes.fix: Always right-click → Run as Administrator, or use an elevated command prompt

mistakes.x: Not running DISM before sfc on heavily corrupted systems
mistakes.fix: If sfc finds errors it cannot fix, run DISM /RestoreHealth first, then rerun sfc

tags: system file checker repair corrupt windows sfc dism image

name: wmic
desc: Windows Management Instrumentation command line. Query hardware and system info.

usage.cmt: all processes with full command line

scenarios: Inventorying hardware before a software deployment
Checking disk health status before a migration
During IR: enumerate startup entries and process command lines

mistakes.x: wmic output is hard to read — pipe to findstr
mistakes.fix: Use | findstr /i "keyword" to filter relevant rows

mistakes.x: wmic is deprecated in Windows 11
mistakes.fix: Use Get-WmiObject in PowerShell for forward compatibility

secnote: Attackers use wmic for lateral movement and persistence: wmic /node:TARGET process call create "cmd.exe". Any unexpected wmic invocations in logs are highly suspicious.
tags: wmic windows management hardware system info process startup inventory

name: ping (Windows)
desc: Test connectivity and latency to a host. Windows ping sends 4 packets by default.

usage.cmt: continuous ping until Ctrl+C — good for monitoring

scenarios: Checking if a server is reachable after a change
Continuous monitoring during a maintenance window
Testing MTU size for VPN or WAN troubleshooting

mistakes.x: Concluding firewall blocks ALL traffic just because ping fails
mistakes.fix: Many firewalls block ICMP specifically — test with telnet host port or tracert

mistakes.x: Windows ping -t running in the background consuming resources
mistakes.fix: Always Ctrl+C or close the window — ping -t runs indefinitely

tags: ping windows connectivity latency icmp test reachability

name: tracert
desc: Windows trace route — shows each network hop to a destination.

usage.cmt: combines ping+tracert — shows packet loss per hop

quick_flags.desc: do not resolve IP addresses to hostnames
max number of hops to search (default 30)

scenarios: Identifying which hop in the path is dropping packets
Confirming traffic is going through expected routes after a network change
Diagnosing VPN routing issues

mistakes.x: Not using -d on slow networks — DNS per hop causes timeout confusion
mistakes.fix: Always add -d; asterisks may be due to DNS timeout not packet loss

mistakes.x: Giving up on * * * hops — some routers don't respond to TTL expiry
mistakes.fix: If final destination responds, intermediate * hops are normal firewall behavior

tags: tracert traceroute hops routing path network windows

name: sc (Service Control)
desc: Query, start, stop, and configure Windows services from the command line.

usage.cmt: list all services and their state

usage.cmd: sc query type= all state= all

usage.cmt: query service configuration (exe path, start type)

usage.cmd: sc failure servicename actions= restart/5000/restart/10000// reset= 3600

scenarios: Service failing — check configuration and executable path before editing in GUI
Configuring automatic restart on failure for a critical service
During IR — disable a compromised service without deleting it

mistakes.x: sc query service with spaces in name fails
mistakes.fix: Wrap names with spaces in quotes: sc query "Print Spooler"

mistakes.x: sc stop doesn't kill child processes
mistakes.fix: Use taskkill /im service.exe /f if sc stop hangs

secnote: Attackers use sc to install malicious services: sc create Malware binPath= "C:\Windows\Temp\evil.exe". Audit sc query output and cross-check paths against known good binaries.
tags: service windows sc start stop configure query control

name: Event Log (wevtutil)
desc: Query Windows Event Logs from the command line without opening Event Viewer GUI.

quick_flags.desc: query events from a log (System, Security, Application)
XPath filter expression for event fields

scenarios: Remote server without RDP — pull logs via command line
Automated log collection in a script
Investigating failed logins on a server during IR

mistakes.x: Opening Event Viewer GUI on a remote server — slow and clunky
mistakes.fix: Use wevtutil qe remotely: add /r:HOSTNAME /u:USER /p:PASS

mistakes.x: Not knowing the key Security Event IDs
mistakes.fix: 4624=logon 4625=failed logon 4720=account created 4732=added to group 4688=process created

secnote: Key Security Event IDs to monitor: 4625 (failed logon), 4720 (new account), 4732 (added to admin group), 4698 (scheduled task created), 7045 (new service installed). These are the top attacker footprints.
tags: event log windows security audit logon wevtutil eventid

name: robocopy
desc: Robust file copy. Far more reliable than xcopy for large transfers, with resume capability.

usage.cmt: /E = all subdirs, /Z = restartable, /LOG = log to file
/MIR = mirror — deletes files in dest not in source, use with care

quick_flags.desc: copy all subdirectories including empty ones
restartable mode — resumes after network drop
mirror — deletes extra files at destination
copy all file info including permissions
list only — no actual copy (dry run)

scenarios: Migrating a file server — robust transfer with full resume on network drop
Backing up user profiles with ACL preservation
Synchronizing directories — scheduled task with /MIR

mistakes.x: /MIR deletes files in the destination not in source
mistakes.fix: Test with /L (list only, no copy) first — /MIR is destructive if source path is wrong

mistakes.x: Not using /Z on large transfers over unreliable networks
mistakes.fix: /Z enables restartable mode — file can resume from where it stopped after a connection drop

tags: copy file transfer robocopy backup mirror windows sync large

name: reg (Registry)
desc: Query, add, delete, and export Windows Registry keys from the command line.

quick_flags.desc: read values from a registry key
create or set a registry value
delete a key or value (force, no prompt)
save a key and subkeys to a .reg file
restore a .reg file into the registry

scenarios: During IR — check classic persistence locations in the registry
Scripting a registry change across multiple machines
Backing up a registry key before making a change

mistakes.x: Editing registry without export backup first
mistakes.fix: Always reg export KEY backup.reg before any edit — one command to restore if it breaks

mistakes.x: reg delete without /f prompts interactively — breaks scripts
mistakes.fix: Add /f for force in scripts to avoid hanging on confirmation

secnote: Top persistence registry locations to check during IR: HKLM\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run, HKCU\...\Run, HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services. Unknown entries = red flag.
tags: registry windows reg run key startup persistence hkey
